feature: Viewer UX step 5: review/challenge/controller panels and run lists

scenarios.description: On a review node a blocking-finding card, outside review-findings and without the finding test id, comes before the findings table; decided reviewers show their duration from launched_at to accepted_at, a print reviewer says 'launch time not recorded', and a pending or superseded reviewer shows 'no verdict' with its launch time and no ticking clock; at 390 px the same findings DOM is restyled as cards with no horizontal overflow and every existing finding count is unchanged

The challenge node opens with one headline (outcome, attempt, notes count, decided time, total span), an attempt strip, P0/P1 concerns open and P2 concerns one line each; a paused challenge shows the P1 in full with the resume and --accept-challenge commands

Handoff shows the wait from the latest launch start to freeze taken from receipts; an approval with no event shows ≈ and 'no approval event recorded'; integrate names the fast-forwarded branch and commit and 'no push performed'; a manual run awaiting approval shows the approve command with the bundle hash

/projects lists Needs you, Running and Recent across all projects, grouped by activity.attention.kind (question, pane, approval) and status, with compact project cards; titles follow the workflow title rule; each row is one link in an li whose accessible name starts with the run id; the project page groups rows by feature; the feature page keeps run-list li rows and moves Current definition into a closed details

The lists and run page read the served activity: a live <lane>.questions.json answered state in the candidate phase; the RUN= line in copied commands when run_dir is served (worker-phase mocks; the candidate phase asserts it absent); the live chip shows 'controller running' from worker-phase mocks, and in both phases 'controller not running' appears only after not_running has held for 15 s (page.clock.install and fastForward)
